title: Candy Boxes
statementMd:
There is an old tradition of keeping $4$ boxes of candies in the house in Cyberland. The numbers of candies are special if their arithmetic mean, their median and their range are all equal. By definition, for a set ${*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}, *x*_{3}, *x*_{4}}$ ($*x*_{1} ≤ *x*_{2} ≤ *x*_{3} ≤ *x*_{4}$) arithmetic mean is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/daeb25d0b520beaea095158d4851903f527ffafc.png), median is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7655b731471163052bb5fbb4c5414c495a2ca2e2.png) and range is $*x*_{4} - *x*_{1}$. **The arithmetic mean and median are not necessary integer.** It is well-known that if those three numbers are same, boxes will create a "debugging field" and codes in the field will have no bugs.

For example, $1, 1, 3, 3$ is the example of $4$ numbers meeting the condition because their mean, median and range are all equal to $2$.

Jeff has $4$ special boxes of candies. However, something bad has happened! Some of the boxes could have been lost and now there are only $*n*$ ($0 ≤ *n* ≤ 4$) boxes remaining. The $*i*$-th remaining box contains $*a*_{*i*}$ candies.

Now Jeff wants to know: is there a possible way to find the number of candies of the $4 - *n*$ missing boxes, meeting the condition above (the mean, median and range are equal)?

## Input

The first line of input contains an only integer $*n*$ ($0 ≤ *n* ≤ 4$).

The next $*n*$ lines contain integers $*a*_{*i*}$, denoting the number of candies in the $*i*$-th box ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 500$).

## Output

In the first output line, print "`YES`" if a solution exists, or print "`NO`" if there is no solution.

If a solution exists, you should output $4 - *n*$ more lines, each line containing an integer $*b*$, denoting the number of candies in a missing box.

All your numbers $*b*$ must satisfy inequality $1 ≤ *b* ≤ 10^{6}$. It is guaranteed that if there exists a positive integer solution, you can always find such $*b*$'s meeting the condition. If there are multiple answers, you are allowed to print any of them.

**Given numbers $*a*_{*i*}$ may follow in any order in the input, not necessary in non-decreasing.**

**$*a*_{*i*}$ may have stood at any positions in the original set, not necessary on lowest $*n*$ first positions**.

## Note

For the first sample, the numbers of candies in $4$ boxes can be $1, 1, 3, 3$. The arithmetic mean, the median and the range of them are all $2$.

For the second sample, it's impossible to find the missing number of candies.

In the third example no box has been lost and numbers satisfy the condition.

**You may output $*b*$ in any order.**
statementZhMd:
Cyberland 有一个古老的传统：在家中存放 $4$ 个糖果盒。如果它们所含糖果数量的算术平均数、中位数和极差都相等，则这些数量就是特殊的。根据定义，对于集合 ${*x*_{1}, *x*_{2}, *x*_{3}, *x*_{4}}$（$*x*_{1} ≤ *x*_{2} ≤ *x*_{3} ≤ *x*_{4}$），算术平均数为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/daeb25d0b520beaea095158d4851903f527ffafc.png)，中位数为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7655b731471163052bb5fbb4c5414c495a2ca2e2.png)，极差为 $*x*_{4} - *x*_{1}$。**算术平均数和中位数不一定是整数。** 众所周知，如果这三个数相等，盒子就会产生一个“调试场”，在其中运行的代码将不会出现 bug。

例如，$1, 1, 3, 3$ 是一组满足条件的 $4$ 个数，因为它们的平均数、中位数和极差都等于 $2$。

Jeff 有 $4$ 个装有糖果的特殊盒子。然而，糟糕的事情发生了！其中一些盒子可能丢失了，现在只剩下 $*n*$（$0 ≤ *n* ≤ 4$）个盒子。第 $*i*$ 个剩余盒子中有 $*a*_{*i*}$ 颗糖果。

现在 Jeff 想知道：是否存在一种方案，确定丢失的 $4 - *n*$ 个盒子中的糖果数量，使得上述条件（平均数、中位数和极差相等）成立？

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$0 ≤ *n* ≤ 4$）。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行包含整数 $*a*_{*i*}$，表示第 $*i*$ 个盒子中的糖果数量（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 500$）。

## 输出格式

在输出的第一行中，如果存在满足条件的方案，输出 "`YES`"；如果不存在，输出 "`NO`"。

如果存在满足条件的方案，还应输出 $4 - *n*$ 行，每行包含一个整数 $*b*$，表示某个丢失盒子中的糖果数量。

所有输出的数值 $*b*$ 都必须满足不等式 $1 ≤ *b* ≤ 10^{6}$。保证如果存在正整数解，就一定能找到满足上述条件的这些 $*b*$。如果有多个答案，可以输出其中任意一个。

**给定的数值 $*a*_{*i*}$ 在输入中可以按任意顺序出现，不一定按非递减顺序排列。**

**$*a*_{*i*}$ 在原集合中可以处于任意位置，不一定位于最前面的 $*n*$ 个位置。**

## 说明

对于第一个样例，$4$ 个盒子中的糖果数量可以是 $1, 1, 3, 3$。它们的算术平均数、中位数和极差都等于 $2$。

对于第二个样例，不可能找到缺失盒子中的糖果数量。

在第三个样例中，没有盒子丢失，并且这些数满足条件。

**你可以按任意顺序输出 $*b*$。**
